title: Batching Orchard: Profile-driven heuristic recommender with cautious apply/rollback
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Implement a production-grade recommendation engine ("Batching Orchard") that continuously profiles request workloads, derives KV/cache-aware batching heuristics and conservative parameter suggestions, and performs safe, observable configuration apply with automatic rollback on regressions. The engine should produce per-route recommendations (batch_size, max_latency_target, kv_window, cache_ttl, microbatch_threshold) and expose a shadow/apply workflow that: runs offline simulations, performs staged shadow deploys, validates SLO/cost/regression signals, then automatically applies or rolls back changes with explanatory rationale and rollback provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry collector emits per-route workload signatures (median/95/99 latency, seq_len distribution, burstiness metric, kv-hit-ratio estimate) every 15m
Recommendation engine produces deterministic suggestions for each route and model variant and stores them in recommendations table with versioning and confidence score
Shadow-probe flow can run a suggested config in shadow mode for a configurable window and collect outcome metrics without impacting live traffic

Automated apply performs canary staged rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with user-configurable guardrails and auto-rollback when any regression threshold is breached (latency p95 increase > 10ms OR error rate increase > 0.5% OR cost-per-token increase > 8% without QoE improvement)
Safety UI surfaces before/after expected cost delta, latency delta, confidence level, and top contributing signals; auditors can pause or force-rollback
End-to-end e2e test coverage for recommender scoring, shadow runs, and rollback trigger logic with synthetic workload generator
tasks: Design workload fingerprint schema (seq_len histograms, inter-arrival CDF, kv-window samples, prompt prefix patterns)
Implement streaming profiler to aggregate 15m window signatures into time-series and snapshot store
Prototype heuristic rules: kv-aware batching (prefer small batches if kv-hit-ratio < 0.3), burst smoothing (auto-decrease batch target during high burst_index), quantization fallback suggestions
Build simulator to replay traces against candidate configs and estimate latency/cost/QoE delta
Integrate shadow-probe runner into routing layer so probes execute on isolated capacity with identical model variant
Implement staged rollout controller with metric guards and automatic rollback policy
Add recommendation API (read/write) with versioning, rationale text, and confidence score
Instrument Console: recommendation listing, per-route recommendation timeline, manual apply/rollback buttons, and explanation links
Create runbook and safety checklist for SRE to audit and intervene
notes: Trade-offs: rule-based heuristics are faster to ship but we will design scoring to allow replacing heuristics with a learned model later
We must ensure shadow probes do not consume reserved/trust capacity for dedicated customers — use isolated probe pool
KV-aware logic requires telemetry from runtime about kv cache hit estimations; fallback to conservative assumptions if telemetry missing
Define user-facing rollback windows and retain previous config history for at least 30 days
